title: A tax exemption rule is added inside the confirmation email builder

consumerGuidance.architecture: Shop.Orders holds order policy. Email bodies are built in the same assembly; marketing changes the templates without developer review of money rules.
consumerGuidance.notes: The persisted order total is written from the value BuildBody returns.

mustCite: the charity tax-exemption rule placed inside BuildBody, which also renders the email
that BuildBody's return value is persisted as the order total, so presentation and money policy are now one responsibility
the consequence that a template edit can change a billed amount, and that the exemption cannot be applied where no email is sent
a proportionate correction that computes the exempt total in order policy and lets the body render the result

forbiddenFindings.example: Reporting that OrderConfirmationService has grown to 90 lines or takes four constructor parameters.
Requiring a Clean Architecture project split, a domain-events pipeline or a templating engine.
Objecting to the raw string literal or to the private helper's name.

notes: The entanglement is concrete because the rendering method's return value is persisted as money, which is what raises this above a taste-level layering objection.
